problem: Radiance-field navigation (e.g. SplatNav) assumes a known, high-quality map, relies on soft Gaussian geometry with convex-corridor planning that fails when goals lie flush against surfaces, and semantic GS methods embed dense features at high cost.
motivation: Robots in unknown indoor scenes need both safe collision avoidance and object-level goals. TSDF gives reliable geometry but no semantics, while GS gives appearance but soft geometry. Lightweight 2D detection lifted through TSDF depth could give semantics without dense 3D embeddings.
key_idea: Build on GSFusion's online TSDF+GS map, lift YOLO 2D detections into 3D via fused depth and DBSCAN clustering into semantic waypoints, and plan smooth B-spline trajectories on TSDF distances with a hinge-based collision loss.
insight: Planning on explicit TSDF distance with a gradient-based B-spline optimizer (A* seeded, hinge plus small exponential term giving non-vanishing gradients) avoids the corridor-generation failures of SFC methods, giving 100% feasibility and far lower jerk. The semantic-target experiment shows the cost: centroids lying inside objects force the spline into the safety margin, so strict GT success drops to 79% versus SplatNav's 99% (on feasible paths only), and margins fall to about 0.01 m. Planning is also slower (0.36 s vs 0.16 s).
method: Semantic 2D inference: YOLOv8n-seg run per frame gives boxes, class labels from language prompts, and confidence scores; exported to ONNX and run via the OpenCV DNN CUDA backend.
Semantic lifting: pixels in each detection are back-projected using GSFusion's fused depth, intrinsics K and camera pose T_WB; the median 3D position of the masked region is the centroid.
Spatial consolidation: points accumulated over multiple views are clustered with DBSCAN, sparse points are rejected as noise, and each cluster gets a centroid and ID as a 3D semantic waypoint.

B-spline parameterization and initialization: a degree-8 uniform B-spline; a 3D occupancy grid with 1.5×r_robot inflation, with start/goal projected to the nearest safe voxel and A* run to seed control points.
Multi-objective optimization: Adam with autograd minimizes w_coll·L_coll + w_dist·L_dist + w_acc·L_acc + w_jerk·L_jerk; L_coll uses TSDF distance in a hinge max(0,1-d/m) plus alpha·exp(-beta·d).
Endpoint truncation: the optimized spline is cut by 1.5×r_robot at both ends and linearly connected to the exact start and goal, because semantic centroids lie inside obstacles.

setting.backbone: YOLOv8n-seg (detector) + GSFusion TSDF/GS mapping; planner is gradient-based optimization (no learned policy)
setting.training_data: none for the planner; pretrained YOLO detector (no additional training described)
setting.observation: RGB-D stream with estimated camera pose
setting.simulator: Replica dataset (offline RGB-D sequences, simulated robot)
setting.privileged: Scenario A uses handcrafted start/goal; GT collision checking is used for evaluation only; camera poses come from the dataset/estimator

numbers.eval_set_note: 7 Replica scenes (office0,2,3,4, room0,1,2); 3 repetitions per scene; handcrafted start/goal
numbers.extra: compared against SplatNav; SplatNav averages exclude office3 where it failed

numbers.eval_set_note: 7 Replica scenes; targets are YOLOv8n-seg lifted semantic instances

numbers_note: Custom planning metrics on Replica, not a standard navigation benchmark; split labelled 'test' as there is no official split. Reconstruction time: GSFusion 439.44s vs Nerfstudio 443.30s (text).
results: On Replica, LiftNav reaches 100% feasibility versus SplatNav's 83% (handcrafted goals) and 80% (semantic targets). Its paths are shorter (LE-Len 4.55 vs 5.73 m; 2.96 vs 3.88 m) and smoother (max jerk 0.15 vs 0.72; 0.11 vs 0.62 m/s^3). It is slower to plan (0.36 vs 0.25/0.16 s) and has lower strict GT success and margin in the semantic setting (79% vs 99%; 0.01 vs 0.20 m).
limitations: Multi-view lifting places centroids deep inside objects, forcing the path through the safety margin and causing GT collisions near targets (79% success).
Evaluated only on Replica in simulation with a single baseline (SplatNav); no real robot, dynamic scenes or outdoor tests.
Slower planning than SplatNav (0.36 s vs 0.16–0.25 s) and not a real navigation benchmark with closed-loop exploration.
